blocks.text: Ab hum pehla inverse trigonometric function banate hain: inverse sine. Tareeqa wahi hai jo 9.1 mein tay hua tha: pehle sine ka graph dekho, phir aisa hissa chuno jahan woh one-to-one aur onto ho, aur phir us hisse ka inverse lo. Chaliye qadam ba qadam chalte hain. Is sabaq ke aakhir tak aap ko teen cheezein pakki ho jani chahiye: \(\sin^{-1}\) ka domain, us ki range, aur us ka graph. Yahi teen cheezein aage har sawal mein kaam aayengi, khaas taur par principal value nikalne mein, is liye inhein sirf ratta na lagaiye balke samajhiye ke yeh kahan se aati hain.

Kitab kehti hai: function \(f : \mathbb{R} \to [-1, 1]\) ko dekhiye jo \(f(x) = \sin x\) se defined hai. Is ka graph Figure 9.1 mein hai. Yahan domain poora \(\mathbb{R}\) hai (har real number angle ban sakta hai), aur codomain \([-1, 1]\) hai, kyun ke sine ki value kabhi \(-1\) se kam ya \(1\) se zyada nahin hoti.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "define by" chhapa hai; sahi "defined by" hai. Yeh grammar ki ghalti 9.1.2 aur 9.1.3 ke shuru mein bhi dohrai gayi hai. Maths par is ka koi asar nahin.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = sin x from minus 4 pi to 4 pi. The wave rises to 1 and falls to minus 1 again and again; dashed horizontal lines y = 1 and y = minus 1 touch it at every maximum and minimum point.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.1: Graph of f(x) = sin x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ab graph ko ghor se dekhiye. Kitab kehti hai: saaf zahir hai ke sine function bijective nahin, kyun ke graph line \(y = 1\) aur \(y = -1\) ko bohat si jagahon par chhoota hai. Is ki wajah yeh hai ke sine ka domain tamam real numbers ka set hai. Lekin agar hum \(f(x) = \sin x\) ke domain ko closed interval \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) tak restrict kar dein, to restricted domain wala function \(f : \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] \to [-1, 1]\) one-one aur onto (yani bijective) ban jata hai. Aisa function invertible hota hai (yani us ka inverse mojood hota hai), aur ise principal sine function kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Figure 9.1 ko horizontal line test se parhiye: line \(y = 1\) graph ko \(\dots, -\frac{7\pi}{2}, -\frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{2}, \dots\) par chhooti hai, yani laatadaad baar. Is liye poore \(\mathbb{R}\) par sine one-to-one nahin. (Bariki ki baat: bijective ya non-bijective function hota hai, graph nahin; graph sirf dikhata hai.)
Ab sawal yeh ke kitab ne bilkul \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) hi kyun chuna? Teen wajahein hain:
1. Is interval mein sine lagataar \(-1\) se barh kar \(1\) tak jata hai. Yani \([-1, 1]\) ki har value sirf ek baar leta hai: one-to-one bhi, onto bhi.
2. Is mein \(0\) aur tamam acute angles \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\) shamil hain, jo hum sab se zyada istemaal karte hain.
3. Negative values ke liye negative angles \(-\frac{\pi}{2} \le \theta < 0\) mojood hain, is liye kisi value ke liye doosre quadrant mein jane ki zaroorat nahin parti.
Misaal: sirhi (staircase) jo sirf upar jati ho, us par har oonchai ek hi seedhi par milti hai. Restricted sine aisi hi sirhi hai jo \(-1\) se \(1\) tak sirf upar jati hai.
Ab jab principal sine function bijective hai, to is ka inverse define kar sakte hain. Kitab ke mutabiq inverse sine function yun defined hai:

blocks.text_alt: y equals sine inverse of x if and only if x equals sine of y

blocks.text: jahan \(\sin^{-1} x\) ka domain \([-1, 1]\) hai aur \(\sin^{-1} x\) ki range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) hai. Dekhiye kya hua: principal sine ka domain \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) tha, woh inverse ki range ban gaya; aur sine ki range \([-1, 1]\) thi, woh inverse ka domain ban gayi. Yahi Recall! box wala rule hai ke inverse mein domain aur range jagah badal lete hain.

blocks.caption: Domain aur range ki adla badli (hamara khulasa)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is table se do kaam ki baatein nikalti hain:
Pehli: \(\sin^{-1} x\) sirf \(-1 \le x \le 1\) ke liye maani rakhta hai. \(\sin^{-1} 2\) mojood hi nahin, kyun ke koi angle aisa nahin jis ka sine 2 ho.
Doosri: \(x\) kuch bhi ho, jawab \(\sin^{-1} x\) hamesha \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke darmiyan hoga. Yeh har jawab ka imtihan (test) hai. Maslan \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{6}\) hai, \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) kabhi nahin, halaan ke \(\sin\frac{5\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\) bhi hai. Wajah: \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) range se bahar hai.
Khud sochiye: \(\sin^{-1}(-1)\) kya hai? (Jawab: \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\), kyun ke \(\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1\) aur \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) range ke andar hai. \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) ka sine bhi \(-1\) hai magar woh range se bahar hai.)

Kitab aage batati hai ke function \(\sin : \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] \to [-1, 1]\) ka graph Figure 9.2(a) mein hai, aur \(\sin^{-1} : [-1, 1] \to \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) ka graph Figure 9.2(b) mein hai. Dono ko saath saath rakh kar dekhiye.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = sin x only from minus pi over 2 to pi over 2. It rises steadily from the point (minus pi over 2, minus 1) through the origin to the point (pi over 2, 1).
blocks.caption: Figure 9.2(a): Graph of y = sin x from −π/2 to π/2 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.alt: Graph of y = inverse sine of x from minus 1 to 1. It rises from the point (minus 1, minus pi over 2) through the origin to the point (1, pi over 2), steep at both ends.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.2(b): Graph of y = sin⁻¹ x from −1 to 1 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono graphs ke end points milaiye: sine wale graph ka point \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, 1\right)\) inverse sine wale graph par \(\left(1, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) ban gaya, aur \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, -1\right)\) ban gaya \(\left(-1, -\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). Yani \(y = \sin x\) ka har point \((a, b)\) graph \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) par \((b, a)\) ban jata hai: coordinates jagah badal lete hain.
Figure 9.2(a) chaurai (width) mein lamba hai (\(-1.57\) se \(1.57\) tak) aur oonchai mein chhota (\(-1\) se \(1\)); Figure 9.2(b) mein bilkul ulta hai. Yeh bhi isi adla badli ka asar hai.
Neeche ki table Figure 9.2(b) ke kuch points deti hai. Har value ek standard angle ko ulta parh kar mili hai, jaise \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) se \(\sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{\pi}{3}\). Negative values ke liye angle bhi negative hai, kyun ke sine ek odd function hai: \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\).

blocks.caption: Principal inverse sine ki kuch values (hamari table; har value [−π/2, π/2] ke andar hai)

blocks.text: Kitab kehti hai ke \(\sin^{-1} x\) ka graph is tarah bhi mil sakta hai ke principal sine function \(y = \sin x\) ke graph ko line \(y = x\) mein aaine ki tarah ulta (reflect) kar diya jaye; yeh Figure 9.3 mein dikhaya gaya hai. Dekhiye ke \(y = \sin x\) aur \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) ke graphs line \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se symmetric hain, yani ek doosre ka aaina hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "is also obtain by reflecting" chhapa hai; sahi "is also obtained by reflecting" hai. Phir kitab likhti hai "Observe that the graph of \(y = \sin x\) is symmetric about the line \(y = x\)". Yeh durust nahin: akela \(y = \sin x\) ka graph line \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se symmetric nahin. Sahi baat yeh hai ke \(y = \sin x\) (principal) aur \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) ke graphs line \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se ek doosre ke aaine (mirror images) hain. Upar hum ne yahi sahi baat likhi hai.

blocks.alt: The principal sine curve from (minus pi over 2, minus 1) to (pi over 2, 1) and the inverse sine curve from (minus 1, minus pi over 2) to (1, pi over 2), drawn together with the dashed line y = x. Each curve is the mirror image of the other in that line.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.3: y = sin x and y = sin⁻¹ x are mirror images in the line y = x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Line \(y = x\) hi aaina kyun hai? Kisi point \((a, b)\) ko line \(y = x\) mein reflect karein to \((b, a)\) milta hai. Yeh bilkul wahi coordinates ki adla badli hai jo upar dekhi. Is liye kisi bhi function ke inverse ka graph us function ke graph ka \(y = x\) mein aaina hota hai. Yeh rule sirf sine ka nahin, har inverse function ka hai.
Figure 9.3 mein ek aur cheez dekhiye: dono curves origin se guzarte hain aur wahan line \(y = x\) ko chhoote hue nikalte hain. Wajah: \(0\) ke qareeb \(\sin x \approx x\) hota hai (choti angles ke liye), is liye \(\sin^{-1} x \approx x\) bhi.
Ghar par try kijiye: graph paper par Figure 9.2(a) banaiye, \(y = x\) line kheenchiye, aur kaghaz ko us line par mor dijiye. Sine ka curve jahan chhapega, wahan \(\sin^{-1}\) ka curve banega.

Kitab ab ek aham baat batati hai. Sine function ko laatadaad intervals mein se kisi bhi ek par restrict kiya ja sakta hai, jaise \(\left[-\frac{3\pi}{2}, -\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), \(\left[\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right]\), \(\left[\frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{2}\right]\), ya aam shakal mein \(\left[n\pi - \frac{\pi}{2}, n\pi + \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). Har interval par range \([-1, 1]\) hai, har interval ki lambai \(\pi\) hai, aur har ek par sine ya to lagataar barhta hai ya lagataar ghatta hai. Is liye har ek par sine one-to-one ban jata hai. Agar koi interval khaas taur par na bataya jaye, to \(\sin^{-1} x\) woh function hai jis ka domain \([-1, 1]\) aur range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Figure 9.1 se tasdeeq kijiye: \(\left[\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right]\) par sine \(1\) se gir kar \(-1\) tak aata hai (strictly decreasing), is liye wahan bhi one-to-one hai aur \([-1, 1]\) ki har value ek baar leta hai. Yani yeh interval bhi inverse de sakta hai, lekin us inverse ke jawab mukhtalif angles honge.
Ab sochiye agar har student apna apna interval chun le to kya hoga? Ek kahega \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{6}\), doosra \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\), aur imtihan mein jhagra ho jayega! Is liye sab ek hi interval par muttafiq (agreed) hain: \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), yani \(n = 0\). Is se milne wali value principal value kehlati hai. Is kitab mein \(\sin^{-1} x\) ka matlab hamesha yahi principal function hai, jab tak koi aur interval na bataya jaye.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: \(\sin^{-1} x \ne (\sin x)^{-1}\) ya \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh Note bohat aham hai. \(\sin^{-1}\) mein \(-1\) koi power nahin; yeh sirf inverse function ka naam hai. Reciprocal \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) to \(\csc x\) hai, jo bilkul alag function hai (9.1.4 mein aayega).
Hamari taraf se misaal (\(x = \frac{1}{2}\)): \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{6} \approx 0.5236\), jab ke \(\frac{1}{\sin(1/2)} \approx 2.0858\) (yahan \(\frac{1}{2}\) radian mein angle hai). Dono saaf alag hain.
Ulajhan kahan se aati hai? \(\sin^{2} x\) ka matlab waqai \((\sin x)^{2}\) hota hai. Lekin sirf index \(-1\) ka yeh khaas matlab hai ke "inverse function". Agar reciprocal likhna ho to \((\sin x)^{-1}\) ya \(\csc x\) likhiye, \(\sin^{-1} x\) nahin.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ab tak ki baat ko teen chhoti misaalon se pakka karte hain. Har ek mein wahi do qadam hain: pehle "iff" se sine wali equation banao, phir range ke andar angle chuno.
(a) \(\sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\): maan lo \(y = \sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), to \(\sin y = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Standard angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) ka sine yahi hai, aur \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai. Is liye jawab \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).
(b) \(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\): \(\sin y = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\). Value negative hai, is liye range ke andar angle bhi negative hoga. \(\sin\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), to \(\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\). Jawab \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\).
(c) \(\sin\left(\sin^{-1} 0.6\right)\): \(\sin^{-1} 0.6\) woh angle hai jis ka sine \(0.6\) hai; us angle ka sine lene se wapas \(0.6\) milta hai. Yani jawab \(0.6\). Yeh Recall! box ka \(f(f^{-1}(y)) = y\) hai. Dhyan dein: ulta \(\sin^{-1}(\sin\theta) = \theta\) sirf tab sahi hai jab \(\theta\) range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein ho. Maslan \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) = \sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{6}\), na ke \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Khud sochiye: kya \(\sin^{-1}\) ka graph kabhi \(y = 2\) tak pahunchta hai? (Nahin; is ki sab se oonchi value \(\frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57\) hai, jo point \(\left(1, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) par milti hai.)
Khud sochiye: \(x\) barhe to \(\sin^{-1} x\) barhta hai ya ghatta hai? (Barhta hai, kyun ke principal sine barhne wala function hai, aur aaina lene se yeh khoobi qaim rehti hai. Figure 9.2(b) mein curve baayen se daayen upar ja raha hai.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Principal sine function: \(\sin : \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] \to [-1, 1]\), jo bijective hai.
2. \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \sin y\); domain \([-1, 1]\), range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).
3. \(\sin^{-1} x\) sirf \(-1 \le x \le 1\) ke liye mojood hai, aur is ki value hamesha \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hoti hai.
4. \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) ka graph principal sine ke graph ka line \(y = x\) mein aaina hai: \((a, b)\) ban jata hai \((b, a)\).
5. \(\sin^{-1} x\) ka matlab \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) nahin.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{5\pi}{6}\) likh dena: \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) interval \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) se bahar hai, is liye principal value nahin.
2. \(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{7\pi}{6}\) ya \(\frac{11\pi}{6}\) likhna: jawab negative angle \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\) hona chahiye.
3. \(\sin^{-1} 2\) ya \(\sin^{-1}(-1.5)\) nikalne ki koshish karna: yeh mojood hi nahin, kyun ke domain \([-1, 1]\) hai.
4. \(\sin^{-1} x\) ko \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) samajh lena.
